title: Cloze test: rainwater harvesting
text:
Read the passage and choose the most appropriate word for each numbered blank.

Water is one of our most precious resources. In many parts of India, people (1) ........ long distances every day to collect it. Rainwater harvesting is a simple way to (2) ........ this problem. Rain that falls on rooftops is collected and stored (3) ........ later use. If every household adopted this practice, the pressure on rivers and groundwater would (4) ........ considerably.

title: Reading comprehension: the banyan tree
text:
The banyan is the national tree of India. Its branches send down aerial roots that grow into the soil and thicken into new trunks, so a single tree can spread over a very large area. The Great Banyan in the botanical garden at Howrah, near Kolkata, covers an area of several acres, and from a distance it looks more like a small forest than one tree.

In villages, the shade of a banyan has long served as a meeting place where elders settle disputes and travellers stop to rest. Because the tree lives for centuries, it is often seen as a symbol of long life and permanence.

title: Cloze test: regular exercise
text:
Read the passage and choose the most appropriate word for each numbered blank.

Regular exercise is good for both the body and the mind. Doctors (1) ........ that adults should be active for at least thirty minutes a day. A brisk walk, a game of badminton or even climbing stairs (2) ........ count. Exercise strengthens the heart and (3) ........ stress. People who exercise also tend to sleep (4) ........ than those who do not.

title: Reading comprehension: the dabbawalas of Mumbai
text:
Every working day, thousands of dabbawalas in Mumbai collect home-cooked lunches from homes and deliver them to offices across the city. The tiffin boxes travel by bicycle, handcart and suburban train, changing hands several times on the way.

The dabbawalas do not depend on computers. Instead, a simple system of coloured marks and numbers painted on each box tells every carrier where it must go. After lunch, the empty boxes are collected and returned to the same homes that afternoon. Business schools have studied the service because mistakes are remarkably rare.
